comparison.comparison: Printed retraction/HLP route agrees with the prereading explicit smooth product S(L)×S1 and central Gysin/Mayer–Vietoris basis. The explicit map [l]↦(l/||l||,log||l|| modlogqZ) and inverse prove the product used in the new derivation. On central K/H, w dies and u survives; the global q-cover and B pullbacks give exactly the three primitive classes. Thus H1 central and local filling generize as Ann(w). Coherent Leray and the exact dx/dy coefficient calculation agree.

Printed real-dimension argument is valid: the real coefficient injection preserves three independent vectors at zero; their constant complex relation extends by the identity theorem, so a chosen generic complex basis remains a basis centrally. The frozen derivation instead exhibits a B class and the q-cover u class and separates them by restricting to the Hopf component. Both constructions give the same fixed product coherent frame, with the explicit iota transport under every Gaussian-integer marking.

The translation gluing acts trivially on fibre coherent cohomology. The same constant frame glues globally; the declared cup-product input gives R2=detR1. Connected fibres and Leray then give hq=(1,2,1,0) and full-fibre surjectivity. All input hypotheses hold for the smooth compact construction with b2=0.

The three displayed annihilator equations have the exact integral kernel Z(1,1,0,-1). Fresh arithmetic proves it is primitive and verifies all coordinate changes. The additional printed count r6,s3,t-prime4 gives6=3−1+4, consistent with the three two-component fibres stated in D2.7; this arithmetic and geometry are directly checked after release.

UCT and exponential sequence give Pic(Y)=H1(Y,O). The smooth-fibre torsion set is iota(Q4); central-fibre torsion is iota(Ann(w_i)⊗Q), a subset by the exact integral/coherent commuting maps. Their union is exactly iota(Q4). Countability gives measure zero and empty interior for this exceptional set; density gives empty interior of its complement. The complement is dense because a nonempty open subset of R4 is uncountable, and has full Lebesgue measure because a countable set has measure zero. This checks the two supplementary final claims as well as the statement.
